paragraphs.notes: Continuation page: the whole body is one unbroken list of substituent terms carried over from the previous page and ending in a semicolon, with no paragraph number (this WO publication prints no [00NN] markers at all) and no sentence of its own except "oder eine der Gruppen" and "und". zh keeps the printed German line breaks and every hyphen exactly as set, including the two hyphens that fall at a line end ("Arylalkoxycarbonyl-" / "amino" and "Heteroaryl-" / "alkoxycarbonylamino"); en runs the list continuously and joins those two words. Every other hyphen shown is mid-line in the original and is reproduced in both fields. The terms are systematic substituent names, so en differs from zh only in the standard German-to-English spellings: Alkinyl -> alkynyl and Halogenalkyl- -> haloalkyl-. Printed as-is and not corrected: "Arylalkinyoxycarbonylamino", "Heteroarylalkinyoxycarbonylamino", "Heterocyclylalkinyoxycarbonylamino" and "Arylalkinyoxy-carbonylamino" all lack the l of -alkinyloxy-, while "Heteroarylalkinyloxycarbonylamino" on the same page has it. "Aryloxycarbonylamino", "Arylalkoxycarbonylamino" and several neighbours appear twice on the page, once in each half of the list; both occurrences are transcribed. In the last three lines the 8, 9, 10 and 11 of R8, R9, R10, R11 are printed as superscripts and the n and m of (CH2)n and (CH2)m as subscripts; they are written inline here. The printed text sets "-CH=N-O-(CH2)n- Aryl" with a space after the hyphen.
